breakfast.name: Medialunas (Crescent Pastries)
breakfast.description: Buttery, crescent-shaped pastries similar to croissants, served with café con leche. A staple of Argentine breakfast.
instructions: Mix flour, salt, sugar, and yeast in bowl
Add water and oil; knead until shaggy dough forms
Incorporate butter using lamination technique (fold and roll method)
Refrigerate dough 30 minutes between each turn (4 turns total)
Roll out dough to 1/4 inch thickness
Cut into triangles, roll up, and curve into crescents
Place on baking sheet and let rise 2 hours
Brush with egg wash
Bake at 400°F for 15-20 minutes until golden brown
Serve warm with café con leche
breakfast.notes: Lamination technique is crucial for flaky layers. Keep butter cold throughout.
breakfast.fun_fact: Medialunas are so integral to Argentine culture that the word literally means 'half-moons.' They're eaten with café con leche at breakfast, which is the traditional Argentine start to the day.
alternatives: Store-bought puff pastry for quick version

breakfast.name: Café con Leche (Coffee with Milk)
breakfast.description: Strong espresso-style coffee mixed with hot milk, served in a large cup. The traditional Argentine breakfast beverage.
ingredients: 1 cup strong brewed coffee (or 2 shots espresso)
instructions: Heat milk in a saucepan until steaming
Brew strong coffee
Pour coffee into large cup or bowl
Slowly pour hot milk into coffee while stirring
Add sugar if desired
Add pinch of salt to enhance flavor
Serve immediately in traditional large cup
breakfast.notes: The ratio is traditionally 50/50 coffee to milk, but adjust to taste.
breakfast.fun_fact: In Argentina, café con leche is not just a beverage—it's a ritual. People dunk medialunas and other pastries into the warm milk-coffee mixture.
alternatives: Espresso only for black coffee version
Added condensed milk for sweeter version

lunch.name: Asado (Grilled Meat)
lunch.description: Argentina's most iconic dish - various cuts of beef grilled over fire. A social gathering centered around amazing meat.
ingredients: Chimichurri sauce (parsley, garlic, oil, vinegar, chili)
instructions: Start charcoal grill or wood fire (medium-high heat)
Let coals burn until white ash forms
Season all meats with salt, pepper, garlic, oregano, and cumin
Place meat racks directly over coals
Cook ribs first (they take longest) - about 45 minutes
Add steaks and sausages - cook 20-30 minutes for medium
Move meat to cooler part of grill for gentle finish
Prepare chimichurri sauce while meat cooks
Meat should have charred exterior and pink interior
Serve with fresh bread, potatoes, and chimichurri
lunch.notes: Asado requires patience and heat management. Don't flip too often - let it develop a crust.
lunch.fun_fact: Asado is more than just a meal in Argentina—it's a cultural event and identity. Argentines are known worldwide for their passion for beef and grilling.
alternatives: Chicken thighs instead of beef for lighter option

lunch.name: Milanesa (Breaded Cutlet)
lunch.description: Thin pounded meat patty, breaded and fried until crispy. Served with lemon and chimichurri.
instructions: Pound meat between plastic wrap until very thin
Season with salt, pepper, and garlic
Set up breading stations: flour, beaten eggs, breadcrumbs
Coat each cutlet in flour, shaking off excess
Dip in beaten egg
Coat completely in breadcrumbs, pressing gently
Let sit 5 minutes for coating to set
Heat oil in skillet over medium-high heat
Fry cutlets 2-3 minutes per side until golden brown and crispy
Serve immediately with lemon wedges and chimichurri
lunch.notes: The key is thin, even pounding and a hot skillet.
lunch.fun_fact: Milanesa is found throughout Latin America but is quintessentially Argentine. It's comfort food served at home and in restaurants everywhere.

dinner.name: Carbonada (Beef and Vegetable Stew)
dinner.description: A hearty stew with beef, vegetables, and fruit. Often served in a hollowed-out pumpkin at celebrations.
instructions: Heat oil in large pot; brown beef on all sides
Add onions and garlic; cook until softened
Add cumin, oregano, and bay leaves; toast for 1 minute
Add tomatoes and broth; bring to boil
Reduce heat and simmer covered for 30 minutes
Add carrots, potatoes, corn, and bell pepper
Simmer for additional 20 minutes
Add zucchini, peaches, and raisins
Simmer final 15-20 minutes until beef is very tender
Season with salt and pepper
Remove bay leaves
Serve hot with crusty bread
dinner.notes: The fruit gives this stew its unique sweet-savory flavor profile.
dinner.fun_fact: Carbonada is traditionally served in a hollowed-out pumpkin shell at parties, making it both a dish and a serving vessel.

snacks.name: Empanadas (Filled Pastries)
snacks.description: Baked or fried pastry pockets filled with seasoned beef, vegetables, or cheese. A beloved Argentine street food.
instructions: Make pastry: Mix flour and salt; cut in cold butter
Add egg yolk and warm water until dough comes together
Refrigerate dough 30 minutes
Make filling: Brown ground beef in skillet
Add onion and garlic; cook until soft
Add cumin, oregano, paprika; toast 1 minute
Stir in raisins and chopped hard-boiled eggs
Season with salt and pepper; cool filling
Roll dough to 1/8 inch thickness
Cut 4-inch circles with glass or cutter
Place 1.5 tbsp filling on each circle
Fold in half, seal edges with fork
Brush with egg wash
Bake at 375°F for 25-30 minutes until golden
Cool slightly and serve hot or room temperature
snacks.notes: Empanadas can be baked or fried. Fried ones are crispier; baked ones are lighter.
snacks.fun_fact: Empanadas are found throughout Spanish-speaking countries, but Argentine empanadas are known for their raisins and hard-boiled eggs, which make them unique.
alternatives: Cheese and vegetable filling for vegetarian version

desserts.name: Dulce de Leche (Milk Caramel)
desserts.description: Thick caramel sauce made from sweetened milk. Used as filling, spread, or topping. Argentina's signature sweet condiment.
instructions: Remove labels from condensed milk can
Place can in pot and cover completely with hot water
Keep water level above the can at all times
Boil for 3-4 hours, continuously adding water to keep can submerged
Allow can to cool completely before opening
Carefully open can and transfer caramel to bowl
Stir in vanilla and salt
Use immediately or store in airtight container
Serve on medialunas, in pastries, or as a spread
desserts.notes: IMPORTANT: Never let the can dry out - it can explode. Keep it fully submerged in water at all times.
desserts.fun_fact: Dulce de leche is considered Argentina's national caramel. The legend says it was invented by accident in the 19th century when a maid forgot a pot of milk on the stove.
alternatives: Use oven method at 425°F for 1 hour in water bath
Store-bought dulce de leche to save time
Made from scratch with milk and sugar (more traditional but longer)

desserts.name: Flan (Caramel Custard)
desserts.description: Silky smooth custard with a caramel topping. A classic Argentine dessert served at special occasions.
instructions: Make caramel: In saucepan, mix 1/2 cup sugar and water
Heat over medium-high heat, swirling pan occasionally
When golden amber, pour into flan dish, coating bottom and sides
In blender, combine eggs, both milks, remaining sugar, vanilla, and salt
Blend until smooth
Pour custard mixture into caramel-coated dish
Place flan dish in larger roasting pan
Pour hot water into roasting pan until it reaches halfway up sides
Bake in water bath at 350°F for 45-50 minutes
Custard should jiggle slightly in center but not be liquid
Cool completely, then refrigerate at least 4 hours or overnight
To serve, run knife around edges and invert onto serving plate
desserts.notes: Water bath ensures creamy custard. Don't overbake or it will become rubbery.
desserts.fun_fact: Flan is a Spanish and Latin American dessert, but it's particularly beloved in Argentina where it's served at birthdays, holidays, and special celebrations.
alternatives: Cinnamon or nutmeg for spiced version
Coconut milk instead of evaporated milk
Store-bought caramel topping to save time

drinks.name: Mate (Herbal Tea)
drinks.description: Traditional South American herbal tea served in a gourd with a shared metal straw. A social and ritualistic beverage.
instructions: Heat water to 160-170°F (below boiling)
Fill gourd 3/4 full with yerba mate leaves
Insert bombilla (metal straw) into the leaves
Pour hot water over leaves slowly
Let steep 30 seconds
First person drinks all liquid in one sip
Pass gourd to next person who refills with hot water
Continue passing gourd clockwise
Refill with water as level drops
Continue until mate loses flavor
drinks.notes: Mate is a social ritual - sharing from one gourd is a sign of friendship and bonding.
drinks.fun_fact: Mate is so important to Argentine culture that it's consumed at any time of day, in any weather, at home, at work, and on the street. It's a symbol of Argentinian identity.
alternatives: Mate cocido (milk-based mate) for different flavor

drinks.name: Malbec Wine
drinks.description: Argentina's signature wine - a full-bodied red wine from Malbec grapes grown in Mendoza region. Known for rich, complex flavors.
ingredients: Malbec grapes from Mendoza or Salta regions
instructions: This is a produced beverage - not made at home typically
Serve at room temperature (16-18°C)
Pour into wine glasses
Let wine breathe for 15 minutes before serving
Pairs well with asado and steak
Best enjoyed with friends
drinks.notes: Argentina produces world-class Malbec wines. Some renowned regions are Mendoza and Salta.
drinks.fun_fact: Malbec is Argentina's pride. Argentina produces over 90% of the world's Malbec wine, and it's become a symbol of Argentine winemaking excellence.
